items.title: Nissan narrows operating loss forecast as turnaround gains traction

featured_image.name: Nissan eyes tapping hot Japan real estate market with HQ ...

items.description:
Nissan announced Thursday it expects a net loss of 650 billion yen ($4.2 billion) for fiscal year 2025 ending in March, as the Japanese automaker continues its sweeping turnaround effort under new leadership. The loss is driven primarily by non-cash charges tied to restructuring under the company's "Re:Nissan" recovery plan.[1][2][3]

The forecast marks a difficult but potentially stabilizing chapter for Japan's third-largest carmaker, which has been battered by an aging vehicle lineup, intensifying competition from Chinese rivals, and the financial impact of U.S. tariffs on imported vehicles.

items.title: EU leaders meet in Belgium to counter economic pressure from U.S. and China

featured_image.name: EU leaders meet to counter pressure from Russia, China and Trump

items.description:
European Union leaders gathered Thursday at the historic Alden Biesen castle in eastern Belgium for an informal retreat aimed at revitalizing the bloc's stagnating economy and forging a united response to mounting pressure from the United States, China, and Russia.

The summit, convened by European Council President António Costa, comes as the 27-member bloc grapples with U.S. President Donald Trump's tariff threats, Chinese export restrictions on critical minerals, and hybrid threats from Moscow. Former Italian Prime Ministers Mario Draghi and Enrico Letta have been invited to present updates on their landmark 2024 reports on EU competitiveness and the single market.[1][2][3]

items.title: Penn State team unveils light-powered computer to cut AI energy use

featured_image.name: Programmable photonic chip uses light to accelerate AI ...

items.description:
As artificial intelligence places unprecedented demands on the world's electricity supply, researchers at Penn State have developed a prototype computer that processes data using light instead of traditional circuitry, a breakthrough they say could slash the energy consumption of AI systems.

The optical computing device, detailed in a paper published Wednesday in the journal Science Advances, routes light through an "infinity mirror" like loop of tiny optical components, encoding data directly into beams of light and capturing the resulting patterns with a microscopic camera. The system can perform complex AI calculations faster and with far less energy than conventional electronic computing.[1][2]

items.title: US energy secretary vows 'dramatic' oil output boost in Venezuela

featured_image.name: Delcy Rodríguez receives the U.S. Secretary of Energy ...

items.description:
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright arrived in Caracas on Wednesday for talks with Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez, marking the highest-ranking American energy official visit to the South American nation in nearly 30 years. The meeting at Miraflores Palace focused on revitalizing Venezuela's struggling oil sector and attracting foreign investment following the recent overthrow of Nicolás Maduro.

Wright promised a "dramatic increase" in Venezuelan oil, natural gas, and electricity production, according to France24. "I am convinced we will witness an extraordinary shift in the future of this nation," Wright told reporters after meeting with Rodríguez. The energy secretary said he and Rodríguez "had frank discussions about the substantial opportunities before us" as well as potential challenges.[1]

items.title: Asian stocks hit record high after US jobs beat expectations

featured_image.name: Asia stocks rise as Nikkei sets fresh record, dollar drops

items.description:
Asian equity markets surged to unprecedented levels on Thursday as stronger-than-expected U.S. employment data boosted optimism about the American economy while simultaneously dimming expectations for near-term Federal Reserve interest rate cuts. The dollar strengthened on the news, weighing on currencies including the Canadian dollar and limiting gains in precious metals.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index climbed 0.65% in Thursday trading, reaching a fresh all-time high and extending its gains for the first six weeks of 2026 to approximately 13%, according to Reuters. Shares in South Korea and Japan reached record levels during early trading, propelled by strength in the technology sector.[1][2]

items.title: DeepMind CEO predicts AI-driven 'golden era' within 15 years

featured_image.name: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis sees "watershed moment" for AI

items.description:
Demis Hassabis, the Nobel Prize-winning CEO of Google DeepMind, has predicted that artificial intelligence will usher in a "new golden era of discovery" within the next 10 to 15 years, transforming medicine, solving the energy crisis, and potentially enabling humanity to venture beyond Earth.

Speaking on the Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry podcast with Fortune Editor-in-Chief Alyson Shontell, Hassabis described a vision of "radical abundance" where AI harnesses the scientific method to tackle humanity's most intractable problems.[1][2]

"In 10 to 15 years, we will enter a new golden age of discovery, akin to a new renaissance," Hassabis said. He predicted that "medicine will not resemble what it is today," with AI enabling personalized treatments and curing major diseases.[1]

items.title: Caribbean reef food chains shortened 70% in 7,000 years, study finds

featured_image.name: 7,000 years of change: How humans reshaped Caribbean coral ...

items.description:
Caribbean coral reef food chains have shortened by 60 to 70 percent compared to their prehistoric state, according to a study published today in Nature, revealing that human activities have fundamentally altered how energy flows through these ecosystems and increased their vulnerability to collapse.

An international team of researchers, led by scientists at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute and Boston College, compared modern Caribbean reefs with fossils from approximately 7,000 years ago found in Panama and the Dominican Republic. They discovered that fish have become 20 to 70 percent less functionally diverse, with species that once occupied distinct dietary niches now competing for the same limited resources.[1][2]

items.title: Bangladesh holds first election since 2024 uprising ousted Hasina

featured_image.name: Is BNP’s Tarique Rahman the change post-Hasina Bangladesh is looking for?

items.description:
Bangladesh heads to the polls on Thursday in its first national election since a student-led uprising toppled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August 2024. More than 127 million voters will cast ballots in 299 constituencies, choosing between the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and an alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, while Hasina's Awami League remains barred from participating.

The election will also feature a simultaneous referendum on the July Charter, a document proposing constitutional reforms including a 10-year lifetime cap for prime ministers and expanded presidential powers. Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus, the Nobel Peace Prize laureate who has led the interim government since Hasina's ouster, urged voters on Monday to support the charter, saying a "yes" vote would build Bangladesh's future "in a more positive way."[1]

items.title: Russia launches 'massive' missile attack on Kyiv, killing one

featured_image.name: Kyiv hit by 'massive' Russian missile, drone attack ...

items.description:
The Ukrainian capital Kyiv came under a "massive" Russian missile attack early Thursday morning, with Mayor Vitali Klitschko reporting that residential and non-residential buildings on both sides of the Dnipro River were hit as explosions echoed throughout the city.

"A mass attack on the capital is still underway," Klitschko said on Telegram, announcing that emergency medical teams had been dispatched to respond to the assault. The attack killed one person and injured four others, including a 9-year-old child, in the Obolonskyi district, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Cisco raises revenue forecast, launches AI networking chip

featured_image.name: Cisco introduces AI networking chip

items.description:
Cisco lifted its annual revenue forecast and unveiled a powerful new networking chip on Wednesday, underscoring how surging demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure is driving growth across its business.

The company now expects fiscal 2026 revenue between $61.2 billion and $61.7 billion, up from prior guidance of $60.2 billion to $61 billion. The raised outlook follows a second quarter in which the networking giant reported record revenue of $15.3 billion, a 10 percent increase compared with the same period last year.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: NASA detects water and organic molecules on interstellar comet

featured_image.name: Comet 3I/ATLAS from beyond solar system carries key molecule ...

items.description:
A cosmic wanderer from beyond our solar system is offering scientists an unprecedented window into how planets form around distant stars. Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, only the third confirmed interstellar object ever observed, has yielded a bounty of discoveries including the first detection of water activity from such an object, along with organic molecules and a distinctive carbon-rich composition that is reshaping our understanding of planetary building blocks across the galaxy.

The findings, announced in studies published this week, suggest that the chemical ingredients for life may be common throughout the cosmos. "When we detect water — or even its faint ultraviolet echo, OH — from an interstellar comet, we're reading a note from another planetary system," said Dennis Bodewits, professor of physics at Auburn University. "It tells us that the ingredients for life's chemistry are not unique to our own."[1]

items.title: Italy approves bill allowing naval blockades against migrant boats

featured_image.name: Italy's Meloni blames organised crime for 'alarming' migrant ...

items.description:
Italy's cabinet on Wednesday approved a bill authorizing naval blockades to halt migrant boats during periods of "exceptional pressure" at the nation's borders, a government source told Reuters. The legislation marks one of the most aggressive measures yet by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's right-wing government to curb irregular migration by sea.[1][2]

Under the draft law, the Italian government could prohibit vessels from entering territorial waters for up to six months in cases involving serious threats to public order or national security. Violators would face fines of up to €50,000, with repeat offenders risking confiscation of their vessels—a provision widely seen as targeting charity-operated rescue ships.[2][1]

items.title: Trump, Netanyahu end White House talks without deal on Iran

featured_image.name: Trump, Netanyahu end meeting with no deal on Iran - The Hill

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with President Donald Trump at the White House on Wednesday for roughly three hours, with Netanyahu expected to convey that the second phase of the Gaza ceasefire "is not moving," according to an Israeli source familiar with the discussions. The meeting, their sixth since Trump returned to office in January 2025, produced no definitive outcomes, Trump wrote on Truth Social afterward.[1][2][3][4]

"There was nothing definitive reached other than I insisted that negotiations with Iran continue to see whether or not a Deal can be consummated," Trump wrote, signaling a focus on U.S.-Iran diplomacy rather than the stalled Gaza framework.[5][1]

items.title: Trump weighs second carrier for Gulf as Iran talks resume

featured_image.name: Trump, Netanyahu to meet at White House in high-stakes talks on Iran, Gaza plan

items.description:
President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that the United States would have to take "something very tough" against Iran if diplomatic efforts fail, as he considers deploying a second aircraft carrier to the Middle East and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu prepares to visit Washington.

In interviews with Axios and Fox Business Network, Trump said Tehran "very much wants to reach a deal" but cautioned that failure to reach an agreement would prompt severe consequences. "Either we make a deal, or we'll have to do something very tough — like last time," Trump told Axios, referencing last June's Operation Midnight Hammer, in which US forces struck three Iranian nuclear facilities at Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan.[1][2]

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $67,000 as 'Tinkerbell effect' fades

featured_image.name: Bitcoin bounce fades as it hovers around $67,000 - CNBC

items.description:
Bitcoin dropped below $67,000 on Wednesday, extending a sharp decline that has wiped roughly 40% from its October peak as investor confidence falters and the cryptocurrency's once-tight correlation with traditional equities weakens.

The world's largest cryptocurrency fell to approximately $66,996 early Wednesday morning before stabilizing near $67,000, according to market data. The decline marks a continuation of the sell-off that began when Bitcoin broke below the $70,000 threshold on February 5, triggering what analysts described as one of the most severe deleveraging events of the current cycle.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: MIT develops magnetic mixer to improve 3D bioprinting

featured_image.name: Magnetic mixer improves 3D bioprinting. MagMix, an onboard ...

items.description:
Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have developed a magnetic mixing device called MagMix that addresses one of the most persistent challenges in 3D bioprinting: cells sinking to the bottom of printer syringes during long print sessions. The system, published February 2 in the journal Device, maintained uniform cell distribution across more than 45 minutes of continuous printing while preserving high cell viability.

The problem is simple gravity. Cells are heavier than the hydrogel "bio-inks" that carry them, causing them to settle during printing. "This cell settling, which becomes worse during the long print sessions required to print large tissues, leads to clogged nozzles, uneven cell distribution, and inconsistencies between printed tissues," explained Ritu Raman, the Eugene Bell Career Development Professor of Tissue Engineering and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at MIT.[1][2]

items.title: CME Group explores world's first rare earth futures contract

featured_image.name: CME hikes precious metal margins again after price swings ...

items.description:
CME Group is developing what would become the first futures contract for rare earth elements, according to three sources with knowledge of the matter who spoke to Reuters on Tuesday. The planned contract would combine neodymium and praseodymium—two critical materials used in electric vehicle motors, wind turbines, fighter jets, and drones—giving Western governments, companies, and financial institutions a new tool to hedge exposure to a market dominated by China.[1][2][3]

Rival Intercontinental Exchange is also exploring rare earth futures but is not as advanced in its planning as CME, two of the sources said. CME declined to comment, and ICE did not immediately respond to requests for comment.[2][1]

items.title: Study links climate change to declining southern right whale births

featured_image.name: Southern right whales are having babies less often, but why ...

items.description:
Southern right whales in Australian waters are having calves less often, with new research revealing that climate change is undermining decades of conservation progress for a species once celebrated as a marine recovery success story.

A major study published February 11 in Scientific Reports found that calving intervals among western Australian southern right whales have increased from an average of three to four years, meaning fewer calves are being born each year. The research, drawing on more than three decades of photo-identification data collected at the Head of the Great Australian Bight, links the reproductive slowdown to declining Antarctic sea ice, changes in oceanic conditions, and reduced availability of prey such as krill.[1][2]

items.title: Netanyahu urges Trump to expand Iran talks beyond nuclear program

featured_image.name: Israel's Netanyahu calls meeting with Trump "very productive"

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is set to meet President Donald Trump at the White House on Wednesday to push for a tougher U.S. stance on Iran's ballistic missile program, arriving just days after Washington resumed direct talks with Tehran for the first time since last year's 12-day war.

Netanyahu's visit marks his seventh face-to-face meeting with Trump since the president took office in January 2025, and his sixth on American soil. The Israeli leader moved up the trip from an originally scheduled February 18-19 visit after U.S. and Iranian officials held nuclear talks in Muscat, Oman on February 6. "I will present to the president our perspectives on the essential principles of the negotiations," Netanyahu told reporters before departing Israel on Tuesday, adding that these principles are "crucial not only for Israel but for anyone who desires peace and security in the Middle East."[1][2][3][4]

items.title: 10 dead, including shooter, in British Columbia school shooting

featured_image.name: Ten dead after mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, lockdown lifted

items.description:
A mass shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in northeastern British Columbia on Tuesday afternoon has left ten people dead, including the suspected shooter, according to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. Approximately 25 additional individuals are being assessed for injuries at a local medical center, marking one of the deadliest school shootings in Canadian history.

The RCMP confirmed that officers responded to reports of an active shooter at the school at approximately 1:20 p.m. local time on February 10. During their search of the building, police located six victims deceased inside the school, along with an individual believed to be the shooter who died from what appears to be a self-inflicted injury.[1][2][3]
